curriculum.scope_limit: Single lesson: partial evidence. Cross-check existing card mapping and NESA content point.

lesson.child_mission: Reading to find information uses skimming for gist and scanning for keywords under headings that match the research question.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same strategy to an unfamiliar topic or audience, then compare the effect of two different choices.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Which heading is most relevant for shadow length: Animal habitats or Sun and light?

FEEDBACK
Sun and light — closer to the question.

CHECK
Reading every word of an unrelated chapter wastes research time.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Using two information texts, skim headings, scan for three keywords from your question and record four relevant facts with page/heading locations.

Write a short reflection describing one specific revision you made and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Reading to find information uses skimming for gist and scanning for keywords under headings that match the research question.
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Using two information texts, skim headings, scan for three keywords from your question and record four relevant facts with page/heading locations. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: Sun and light — closer to the question. Reasoning: I used skim by attending to scan and explain why it matters rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Reading every word of an unrelated chapter wastes research time. Correction: Sun and light — closer to the question. Why: the correction restores accurate use of skim.

Parent: Likely misconception: Reading every word of an unrelated chapter wastes research time. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating skim on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with skim, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Require independently produced work with a specific supporting detail. / Require misconception + correction + purpose-linked reason..

teach_steps.explain:
Reading to find information uses skimming for gist and scanning for keywords under headings that match the research question.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
